cim: US artificial intelligence chipmaker Q3 earnings beat forecasts as revenue surges 103%
cim_eredeti: US artificial intelligence chipmaker Q3 earnings beat forecasts as revenue surges 103%
szoveg_eredeti:
A leading US artificial intelligence chipmaker reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings above expectations, supported by continued demand for AI computing infrastructure and expansion of its Data Center business.

Revenue reached $115.8 bn for the quarter ended October 25, 2026, up 103% from $57 bn a year earlier and approximately 20% from the previous quarter.

Adjusted earnings per share increased to $2.68, compared with $1.30 in the year-earlier period. Analysts had expected revenue of $109.15 bn and earnings of $2.47 per share.

The company also reported continued growth in earnings and profitability, supported by sales of high-performance processors and AI infrastructure systems.

Shares initially advanced following the earnings release but were little changed in early Wednesday trading.

The results were the first quarterly report since the company’s chief executive resigned on November 12. The chief financial officer has assumed the interim CEO position while the board searches for a permanent successor.

The Data Center division generated $107.6 bn in quarterly revenue, exceeding the $101.85 bn consensus forecast.

The business accounted for approximately 93% of total quarterly sales, demonstrating the company’s substantial exposure to artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

Demand for advanced AI processors, networking equipment and integrated computing systems remained the principal source of growth.

Major cloud infrastructure providers continued investing in systems designed to support AI model training and inference. The company also reported expanding adoption of its latest CPU architecture among cloud operators and AI developers.

Management expects total CPU revenue to double in fiscal 2028 as demand for processors increases alongside AI accelerators. Outside the Data Center division, Edge Computing revenue reached $8.2 bn, compared with analysts’ expectations of $7.49 bn.

The segment benefited from demand for computing hardware used in applications outside centralized data centers.

The chipmaker expects fourth-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of approximately $130 bn, plus or minus 2%. That implies a range of $127.4 bn to $132.6 bn, compared with analysts’ previous forecast of $125.25 bn.

The guidance indicates continued sequential revenue growth, supported by demand for AI infrastructure products.

The company also maintained its focus on expanding production capacity and meeting customer orders for advanced computing systems.

Management said its outlook assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China. During the earnings call, the company disclosed approximately $2.4 bn in third-quarter revenue from sales of its previous-generation computing platform to China but said shipments to the country had stopped.

Export restrictions and regulatory requirements continue to affect the company’s ability to supply certain advanced processors to Chinese customers.

Management increased its fiscal 2028 revenue growth forecast to 75% year over year, compared with its previous projection of 70%. The company also reported that its cloud industry revenue backlog had reached approximately $2.5 tn, up from $2 tn three months earlier.

The backlog reflects anticipated future demand and commitments associated with AI infrastructure rather than revenue already recognized.

The expansion comes alongside substantial supplier purchasing agreements, customer financing arrangements and equity investments.

According to financial media calculations, combined purchasing, investment and financing commitments approached $670 bn during the quarter, compared with approximately $530 bn in July.

Much of that exposure relates to chips and other components secured through supplier arrangements, particularly memory products. The company also guaranteed approximately $118 bn of financial obligations held by other businesses, including nearly $10 bn in new commitments involving undisclosed partners.

Equity investments in other companies approached $16 bn, with much of the capital directed toward privately held businesses.

Management said future investments, commitments and guarantees would be evaluated as the market matures and additional financing sources become available.

Financial guarantees supporting specialized cloud infrastructure providers generally become effective only after those companies obtain the financing necessary to develop their data center facilities.

The rapid increase in sales has been accompanied by a rise in outstanding customer payments. Accounts receivable reached approximately $81 bn, equivalent to 64 days of sales. That represented the slowest payment collection pace since the semiconductor market downturn in 2022.

Receivables measure revenue recognized but not yet collected in cash, making them relevant to assessing working capital requirements and the financial position of customers.

The increase does not necessarily indicate payment defaults. It does, however, warrant monitoring alongside revenue growth, supplier obligations and financing commitments.

Investors are also assessing the financial sustainability of infrastructure developers undertaking large capital expenditure programs to expand AI computing capacity.

The company announced an additional $150 bn authorization for share repurchases. The expanded program provides additional capacity to return capital to shareholders through stock buybacks.

The authorization follows another quarter of substantial revenue and earnings growth, supported by demand for AI processors and related infrastructure.

Share repurchases can reduce outstanding share counts and support earnings per share, although the financial effect depends on the volume and timing of purchases.

The company continues balancing shareholder distributions with major investments in production capacity, supply agreements and the broader AI computing ecosystem.

The earnings release followed the resignation of the company’s long-serving chief executive on November 12. The board said the departure occurred after disclosures of personal conduct that conflicted with corporate standards.

Directors unanimously accepted the resignation and stated that they did not intend to reinstate the former executive. The chief financial officer has taken over as interim CEO while the board evaluates internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement.

An executive search firm has been retained to assist with the process. During the earnings call, management emphasized continuity in product development, customer relationships and the company’s multiyear technology roadmap.

The board also established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee comprising independent directors, senior external advisers and legal counsel.

The leadership change has created questions about succession planning and strategic continuity at a time when AI infrastructure investment remains substantial.

Nevertheless, the latest quarterly results indicate that customer demand has remained strong during the management transition.

Shares of several semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies advanced in after-hours trading following the earnings announcement.

Two major US semiconductor competitors gained more than 1%, while a leading Asian contract chip manufacturer rose approximately 2%.

The market response reflected stronger-than-expected quarterly results and the higher revenue outlook for the coming periods.

Investors will continue monitoring demand for AI infrastructure, the company’s expanding financial commitments, customer payment cycles and the appointment of a permanent chief executive.

Tetiana Mykhailova is Senior Investment Analyst and CFO of Beinsure, and Commercial Director of Finance Media. She has more than 20 years of experience in hedge finance, investment, data analytics, strategic management, and accounting.
